evals.name: discovery-outline
evals.prompt: i've been building a custom auth system for our b2b saas (~3k prod accounts, employee-managed orgs) for about 3 months. started on auth0, hit hard rate limits and a weird edge case on the org-switching flow where session JWTs would get out of sync, briefly tried clerk but their pricing tier didn't make sense for our shape (we have a lot of low-revenue orgs with high seat count), finally landed on lucia v3 + postgres + redis for sessions. been wanting to write about it but i don't know what the angle is. probably 2000-3000 words on https://eng.acme-co.dev. help me find the kernel and outline it.
evals.expected_output: A discovery + outline response: kernel statement, 1-3 angle options, structured outline with H2s, SEO/GEO/AEO checkpoints annotated, and at least one section explicitly on what didn't work.
assertions: Response opens by stating which mode it is operating in (Discovery, Outline, or both)
Identifies a specific narrative kernel that references at least 2 concrete details from the user's prompt
Offers at least 2 distinct angle options for the article
Provides an outline with at least 5 H2-level sections
Outline includes at least one section explicitly devoted to what didn't work (auth0 limits / clerk pricing mismatch)
Outline includes a direct-answer paragraph slot near the top
Outline includes a FAQ section near the end with question-phrased H3s
Outline references SEO/GEO/AEO scaffolding
Performs an authenticity check
Lists open questions or details the user still needs to resolve before drafting
Does not write polished prose for the article body

evals.name: optimize-draft
evals.prompt:
here's a draft i wrote — can you optimize it for SEO, GEO, and AEO? we're publishing on our company blog (https://api-co.dev/blog) and i want it to actually rank and get cited by AI search engines. the topic is migrating from REST to GraphQL.

draft starts here:
---
# Why We Moved to GraphQL

We migrated our API from REST to GraphQL in Q3. Here's why and how.

## The Problem

Our REST API had a lot of endpoints. Customers were complaining about over-fetching. We had multiple endpoints for similar things.

## The Solution

We adopted Apollo Server. We wrote schemas. We migrated endpoints over a few months.

## Results

Things are better now. Latency is down. Customer feedback has been positive.

## Conclusion

GraphQL is great. We recommend it.
---
end of draft. tell me what's wrong and rewrite the structure to fix it. i can fill in the prose myself.
evals.expected_output: An audit/optimize response with: in-line annotations identifying problems, an annotated rewrite of the structure (not full prose), scores for SEO/GEO/AEO, and a top-3 priority fix list.
assertions: Response opens by stating which mode it is operating in
Identifies that the draft has no direct-answer paragraph at the top and recommends adding one
Identifies the title 'Why We Moved to GraphQL' as generic / lacking the kernel
Flags the absence of any section on what didn't work / approaches that failed
Flags the absence of outbound authoritative citations
Flags the absence of a FAQ section
Mentions schema markup that should be emitted
Provides numeric scores for SEO, GEO, and AEO dimensions
Provides a prioritized fix list
Recommends question-phrased H2s where natural
Recommends specific original-data inclusions
Provides a rewritten outline structure (not full prose)
Does not insert AI prose into the draft

evals.name: visuals
evals.prompt:
writing a deep-dive about how we built a real-time collaboration feature for our document editor using CRDTs (specifically yjs). need two visuals:

1. a hero image for the article — something visually interesting that captures 'real-time collaboration with conflict resolution', not literal screenshots
2. an architecture diagram showing 4-5 connected clients <-> websocket server <-> postgres for snapshots, with the yjs awareness protocol shown somehow

what should i do for each? give me the actual SVG for the diagram, and a JSON spec for the hero so i can hand it to dall-e or midjourney.
evals.expected_output: Two visuals: (1) JSON image spec for hero with all required fields, (2) inline SVG for architecture with <title>/<desc> and text labels.
assertions: Response opens by stating which mode it is operating in (Visuals)
Produces a JSON image specification for the hero image
Hero JSON spec includes purpose, context, subject, style, color_palette, aspect_ratio, include, exclude, mood, alt_text, tools_supported
Hero JSON spec's color_palette is an array of hex codes
Hero JSON spec's exclude list contains text/logos/watermarks
Hero JSON spec is saved as a separate file at hero-spec.json
Produces inline SVG markup for the architecture diagram
SVG includes a <title> element
SVG includes a <desc> element
SVG uses <text> elements for labels (not paths)
SVG visually shows at least 4 client elements
SVG visually shows a websocket server element
SVG visually shows postgres / database element
SVG indicates the yjs awareness protocol
Architecture SVG is saved as a separate file at architecture.svg
Response explains the SVG-vs-JSON decision
